title: Tokenization and Vocabulary Design
summary: Tokenization maps text or other symbolic inputs to discrete model units. A good vocabulary balances sequence length, coverage, reversibility, multilingual behavior, and implementation cost.

title: Pretraining Data, Cleaning and Mixtures
summary: Pretraining quality depends on what enters the mixture, how examples are cleaned and deduplicated, and how sampling weights evolve during training.

title: Embeddings, Retrieval and Reranking
summary: Retrieval systems separate fast candidate generation from more expensive relevance scoring. Sparse, dense, hybrid, and reranking stages solve different failure modes.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: RAG combines retrieval, context construction, and generation. The system is only as reliable as its evidence selection, authorization boundary, prompt design, and evaluation decomposition.

title: LLM Inference: Prefill, Decode and KV Cache
summary: Autoregressive inference has a parallel prefill phase and a sequential decode phase. KV caching avoids recomputing past key and value projections while preserving attention over the prefix.

title: LLM Serving and Request Scheduling
summary: Serving turns model inference into a multi-tenant scheduling and memory-management problem. Throughput, time to first token, inter-token latency, fairness, and reliability often conflict.

title: Distributed LLM Training
summary: Distributed training partitions data or model state while coordinating mathematically equivalent updates. Correctness depends on collective order, data ownership, numerical scaling, and restart semantics.

title: Tensor, Pipeline, Context and Expert Parallelism
summary: Model parallelism partitions work that cannot fit or run efficiently on one device. Tensor, pipeline, context, and expert dimensions introduce different communication patterns.

title: Distributed LLM Inference
summary: Distributed inference partitions weights, layers, experts, context, or requests. The correct design depends on whether the primary constraint is memory capacity, latency, throughput, or availability.

title: RoPE and Positional Extrapolation
summary: Rotary positional embeddings encode relative position by rotating query and key subspaces with position-dependent phases.

title: Long-Context Modelling
summary: Long-context systems must manage attention cost, KV memory, positional generalization, data quality, and evaluation over distant dependencies.

title: Mixture-of-Experts Models
summary: MoE layers activate a small subset of experts per token, increasing parameter capacity without proportional dense compute.

title: Post-Training: SFT, Reward Models, PPO, DPO and GRPO
summary: Post-training adapts a pretrained model to instructions, preferences, safety constraints, and task-specific behavior using supervised and preference-based objectives.

title: Reasoning Training, RLVR and Test-Time Compute
summary: Reasoning systems combine data, objectives, search, verification, and inference-time compute. Longer outputs alone do not establish better reasoning.

title: LLM Evaluation and Benchmark Design
summary: Evaluation should connect a model or system change to decisions under representative data, uncertainty, cost, and failure constraints.

title: Hallucination, Grounding and Calibration
summary: Calibration asks whether stated or derived confidence matches empirical correctness. Grounding asks whether claims are supported by permitted evidence.

title: Tool Calling and Structured Outputs
summary: Tool use introduces an execution boundary: the model proposes actions, while deterministic software validates, authorizes, executes, and records them.

title: Agents, Orchestration and Agent Evaluation
summary: An agent is a policy over observations, model calls, tools, state, and stopping decisions. Reliability comes from explicit orchestration and bounded authority.

title: Quantization, Pruning and Distillation
summary: Compression reduces model memory, bandwidth, or compute by lowering precision, removing structure, or training smaller models to match larger ones.

title: Speculative Decoding and Inference Acceleration
summary: Speculative decoding uses a cheaper proposal process and a target model that verifies several candidate tokens while preserving the target distribution under the exact algorithm.

title: Multimodal Transformers
summary: Multimodal models align representations and generation across text, image, audio, video, or sensor inputs with modality-specific encoders and fusion mechanisms.

title: Encoder-Decoder Models and Cross-Attention
summary: Cross-attention lets one sequence query representations from another. Encoder-decoder models use it to condition generation on a separately encoded source.

title: State-Space Models and Alternative Sequence Architectures
summary: State-space sequence models propagate a compact state through time and can admit recurrent, convolutional, or scan-based implementations.

title: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training
summary: Scaling laws model how loss or capability changes with parameters, data, and compute over a measured regime. They support planning but do not replace pilot experiments.

title: Synthetic Data Generation and Filtering
summary: Synthetic data can expand coverage, generate verifiable tasks, distill behavior, or rebalance rare cases, but it can also amplify model errors and reduce diversity.

title: torch.compile, Custom Kernels and GPU Performance
summary: GPU performance work connects model graphs, compiler transformations, kernels, memory traffic, launch overhead, and numerical constraints.

title: LLM Security, Prompt Injection and Data Leakage
summary: LLM security treats model inputs, retrieved content, tools, memory, and outputs as parts of a larger trust-boundary system.

title: Probabilistic Modelling Foundations
summary: Probabilistic modelling specifies random variables, distributions, conditional structure, and inference questions rather than only point predictions.

title: Uncertainty Quantification
summary: Uncertainty quantification represents and evaluates predictive uncertainty, separating irreducible observation noise from uncertainty caused by limited knowledge.

title: Bayesian Deep Learning and Variational Inference
summary: Bayesian learning places a distribution over unknown parameters or functions. Variational inference approximates an intractable posterior with a tractable family.

title: Gaussian Processes
summary: A Gaussian process defines a distribution over functions through a mean function and positive-semidefinite kernel.

title: Hidden Markov and Probabilistic State-Space Models
summary: State-space models represent latent dynamics and noisy observations. Hidden Markov models use discrete latent states; linear Gaussian models yield Kalman filtering.

title: Stochastic Processes and SDEs
summary: A stochastic process is a collection of random variables indexed by time or another domain. SDEs combine deterministic drift with stochastic diffusion.

title: Sequential Monte Carlo and Particle Filters
summary: Particle filters approximate sequential posteriors with weighted samples that propagate, reweight, and resample over time.

title: Diffusion and Score-Based Generative Models
summary: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process or estimate the score of intermediate distributions.

title: Energy-Based Models
summary: An energy-based model assigns low energy to preferred configurations and defines a normalized density when the exponential energy is integrable.

title: Flow Matching and Rectified Flows
summary: Flow matching trains a time-dependent velocity field by regression and samples by solving an ODE from a base distribution to data.

title: Normalizing Flows
summary: Normalizing flows transform a tractable base distribution into a target while retaining likelihood evaluation through change of variables.

title: Path Signatures and Rough Paths
summary: A path signature is the ordered collection of iterated integrals of a path and provides a systematic feature representation for sequential data.
